title: Water + ethanol + cyclohexane, NRTL, 30 stages and a decanter: ethanol with 12 mol % water and 3.3 mol % cyclohexane, the organic liquid refluxed, 0.1 mol % water in the bottoms (near-dry ethanol)
purpose: Proposal 0025, step 2 (the maintainer, 2026-11-18): the dehydration column specified by the bottoms purity, 0.1 mol % water (the mole basis, as the column's balances and the decanter's lever rule are molar; about 0.04 mass %). The feed's cyclohexane is 3.3 mol %, not 1.17 %: on the branch the engine reaches the decanter's distillate carries cyclohexane and water in a ratio of about 0.27, so dry bottoms need at least that ratio in the feed (12 % water: 3.25 % cyclohexane); with less, the bottoms run out of cyclohexane before their water reaches 0.1 % (docs/decisions/2026-11-18-07-purity-in-mesh.md). Near-dry ethanol, not anhydrous: 0.14 mol % cyclohexane stays in the bottoms.
method_choice: docs/METHOD_SELECTION.md rules 3 and 7: polar, below 10 bar, two liquids: NRTL with the default sets, each fitted to open measured data (ethanol + water fitted-kamihama2012; water + cyclohexane fitted-marche2006-etal, mutual solubilities; ethanol + cyclohexane fitted-reddy2013; src/data/binaries.json), ideal-gas vapour. None was fitted to ternary data.

behaviour: the column converges with the purity among the MESH equations, from the entrainer start
the reference's profile, liquids and duties within F1's tolerances
the bottoms purity met: the reference writes the same specification row, ln(x / value) = 0
expected.branch: The engine's solution from its entrainer start, the bottoms purity among the MESH equations (proposal 0025, step 2). Heterogeneous azeotropic columns can have several steady states at one specification (docs/decisions/2026-11-18-03-entrainer-start.md); this is the one the start reaches. The reference (validation/python/reference_mesh_vll.py --purity, ChemSep's three-phase stage) solves its own equations, with its own purity row, from the engine's profile, perturbed.

engine_against_reference.why: Proposal 0015, Engineering basis: flows within 1e-6 relative of the independent MESH solution. Both solve the same equations to residuals of 1e-8 or less, so the difference is the solvers' convergence only.

balances_on_every_stage.why: Proposal 0015: every stage's balances closed to 1e-8. Material: |residual| / F; energy: |residual| / (F x 10 kJ/mol); summation and equilibrium are mole fractions.

stability.why: one-liquid stages: no trial liquid on a grid has a tangent-plane distance below -1e-9

agreement_with_data.note: The three NRTL sets are fitted to vapour-liquid data; their liquid-liquid split is W1's work (joint fits, M2b) and not a test of the column.
